source.citation: 36 direction horizon computed at the site coordinates 34.13600 N 77.54700 E from AWS Terrain Tiles (Terrarium encoding), built from SRTM, GMTED and other open elevation data: zoom 12 tiles within 6 km and zoom 9 tiles out to 50 km, 160 samples per direction, with earth curvature and standard refraction
source.note: Replaces the Layer 0 horizon_36dir.csv table, which its own source.txt records as computed at 34.16 N 77.58 E, about 4.0 km from this site. That table blocked the sun to 7.5 degrees on average against 6.6 here, and by up to 5.8 degrees in one direction. The elevation model reads 3257 m at the site against the 3256 m the site record carries from Layer 0; the horizon angles are computed from the model's own value so ground and skyline agree.

source.citation: EPW IND_JK_Leh.427053_TMYx.2011-2025.epw from Climate.OneBuilding.org, source tag SRC-TMYx
source.note: Weather, terrain and ground temperatures all come from the Layer 0 delivery.

source.citation: Undisturbed earth temperature at 0.5 m from the EPW GROUND TEMPERATURES header, calculated from this weather file
source.note: NASA POWER TSOIL1 for 2015 to 2024 is also in the Layer 0 delivery and gives -8.9, -8.5, -7.4, -2.4, 2.8, 7.7, 12.3, 11.9, 7.2, 0.5, -4.4, -8.8 C. It was not used because it is a MERRA-2 reanalysis cell whose grid elevation is 4533 m against the 3256 m of the site, so it does not describe this ground. The EPW header values are derived from the same weather year the simulation runs on, so they stay consistent with it.
